page_title: Steering Claude Code: when to use CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and subagents

sources.entry: Steering Claude Code: Skills, Hooks, Rules, Subagents and More by Anthropic - A framework for choosing which extension mechanism to reach for, organized around deterministic-versus-probabilistic control and context isolation.

summary.name: Steering Claude Code
summary.one_liner: An Anthropic blog post giving a decision framework for choosing among seven ways to instruct Claude Code (CLAUDE.md files, rules, skills, subagents, hooks, output styles, and system-prompt appends) based on context cost, compaction behavior, and authority.
keywords: when to use hooks vs claude.md
use_cases: Deciding where to put team coding conventions
Setting up deterministic automation like linters after edits
Blocking dangerous commands in a coding agent
Offloading deep search or log analysis to isolated subagents
Packaging deploy or review procedures as reusable skills
Scoping API-specific rules to certain directories
summary.what_it_does: The page compares seven methods for instructing Claude Code and summarizes when each loads into context, how it survives compaction, and its context cost. CLAUDE.md files load at session start and stay for the whole session, while subdirectory files load on demand. Rules can be path-scoped with a paths field so they load only for matching files. Skills expose only name and description until invoked, and subagents run in isolated context windows returning just a final summary. Hooks fire on lifecycle events such as PreToolUse and can deterministically block or automate actions, and the post also explains that output styles and appended system prompts change instructions at different authority levels.
notable: Table comparing load timing, compaction behavior, and context cost for each method
Guidance that deterministic guardrails need hooks or managed settings, not CLAUDE.md instructions
Warns that custom output styles can remove Claude Code's default software-engineering instructions
caveats: Advice that output styles and long appended prompts carry adherence trade-offs and should be used sparingly
Managed settings for organization-wide enforcement are described as admin-deployed, so individual users cannot override them
